tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Is this domain what it claims to be? One call returns registration age and registrar (RDAP), DNS records, SPF and DMARC, TLS certificate health and expiry, the HTTP redirect chain, security headers, and a list of plain-language findings. Use it to vet a merchant, sender or link before trusting it. L

tools.name: read_url
tools.description: Fetch a public web page and get its main content as clean Markdown: title, description, language, publish date and the article text with headings, lists, tables, code blocks and links, without navigation, ads or scripts. Built for LLM agents that need to read a URL. Respects robots.txt; static HTML

tools.name: email_auth
tools.description: Can mail from this domain be spoofed? Returns MX, the SPF record and how strict it is, the DMARC policy, DKIM keys found under common selectors, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI, with a spoofable verdict and findings. Use it to judge a sender's domain or audit your own before sending. Live DNS lookups. 5 f

tools.name: tls_certificate
tools.description: Live TLS handshake with a host on port 443: whether the certificate is trusted, who issued it, the names it covers, the protocol version, the expiry date and days left. Use it to catch an expiring or misissued certificate. 5 free calls per day across all tools; pass `key` to use a prepaid balance (0

tools.name: domain_registration
tools.description: Structured registration data for a domain from RDAP, the successor to WHOIS: registrar, creation, expiry and last-changed dates, age in days, status flags, nameservers and whether DNSSEC is signed. Use it to spot a newly registered or soon-to-expire domain. 5 free calls per day across all tools; pas

tools.name: create_key
tools.description: Create an API key and get instructions for funding it with USDC on Base. Only needed beyond the free limit.

tools.name: claim_deposit
tools.description: Credit a key after sending USDC on Base. The amount's last four decimals must be the key's tag.

tools.name: balance
tools.description: Remaining balance of an API key.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_url · Private data: check_domain, email_auth, create_key, balance · Public sink: read_url, email_auth.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_url · Private data: check_domain, email_auth, create_key, balance · Public sink: read_url, email_auth

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
